acceptance: Eviction keeps the resolved tip, the rev named by `last`, and the newest N revs by mtime per namespace; it never deletes the rev `last` names.
The sweep is best-effort and capped per call, guarded by a non-blocking flock, and renames each victim into a trash directory before removing it; it is idempotent so leaked trash self-heals.
Snapshots are written to a temporary directory and renamed into place, so a partial rev cannot exist.
_offline_cached re-reads `last` and retries once before failing.
A one-time bulk prune is an explicit command (or throttled background pass), never part of read().
Multi-process tests cover: concurrent read() calls during a sweep, a sweep during save_snapshot, and an offline read after eviction.
Optional: normalize the remote string in namespace() only with a migration plan for existing namespaces.

description:
read() caches every new state-branch tip as a full snapshot under <cache>/<ns>/revs/<sha>/ and never deletes old ones. Only the resolved tip and the rev named by `last` are ever read back, so the rest is dead weight. The BenchBox namespace (e688dcd1868ed3f8) held 1,508 revs, about 40 GiB, on 2026-10-16 and grows by up to about 3 GiB a day.

An adversarial review rejected the first proposal (keep only the new tip and the previous `last`): the first sweep would delete ~40 GiB inside read() and exceed the git and MCP timeouts; `last` is written by every process and is not monotonic, so the rule can delete the true newest tip; deleting a rev while another process is in save_snapshot raises a raw FileNotFoundError out of read(); _offline_cached has no fallback for a missing or partial rev.
